text:
maria: heads-up, attached a perfetto + nsys capture for the KV-prefetch latency spikes we saw on prod-rt-05. timeline shows tons of tiny H2D transfers interleaved with kernel launches, NVLINK bandwidth looks fragmented. link: https://perfetto.example/trace/abc123 and nsys: gs://redwood-traces/1799004321-rt05.nsys

jordan: saw this earlier on a dev rig too. suspect pinned pool exhaustion -> fallback to pageable which fragments transfers?

lee: quick summary from the trace: sustained NVLINK utilization ~40% but tail latency for small requests spikes 4-10x. lots of `cudaMemcpyAsync` short bursts (~8KiB-64KiB) on stream 7.

sara: attached a perf log snippet: ```
[H2D memcpy] size=16384 start=12.345ms end=12.351ms stream=7 pinned=true host_ptr=0x7f8c...
[kernel] name=kv_prefetch idx=42 start=12.352ms end=12.412ms
[H2D memcpy] size=8192 start=12.413ms end=12.415ms host_ptr=0x7f8c... pageable_fallback=true
```

maria: exact — the allocator below threshold was returning pageable pages for some prefetches. perfetto shows NVLINK had many small windows between kernels, causing queueing and extra latency.

jordan: interestingly, when we injected a pinned-buffer-reserve (10MB/gpu) the small-transfer tail improved dramatically in the dev traces. can we replicate on prod after hours?

lee: i also noticed our batching heuristic issues: prefetcher emits a prefetch per token when cache miss, rather than grouping keys for the same model step. that multiplies H2D ops. suggested changes: 1) aggregate prefetches per request window (<=2ms) 2) prefer coalesced host buffers 3) hold a small pinned slab pool per-GPU and fallback only when exhausted.

sara: test patch: `prefetcher.batch_window_us = 2000` + pinned slab pool PR #4982. ran on canary — nsys shows 70% fewer memcpy ops and 2.8x reduction in 99th H2D latency.

infra-bot: deploy:canary started by @sara to prod-rt-canary-02 at 2026-03-17T02:14:03Z :rocket:

maria: good, also thread notes: we should add an allocator metric (pinned_pool_available_bytes) to console, and a dashboard for small-transfer-rate (<=64KiB) on NVLINK vs PCIe. that will help spot regression.

jordan: for follow-ups: - add unit/integration test that simulates rapid sequence of misses to ensure batching groups prefetches - validate pinned slab reserve default (10MB) across instance types - doc change for runtime tuning and hostalloc flags (cudaHostAllocPortable|WriteCombined?)

lee: one more gotcha: perfetto shows occasional D2H bursts overlapping with H2D windows on same link when we do async D2H reclaim of evicted KV pages. recommend serializing reclaim on a low-priority stream to avoid competing with prefetch H2D.

sara: agree. i'll queue the reclaim-stream-change + metrics PRs. thanks for quick triage. :thumbsup:

maria: great work team — capture saved the day again. tagging @eng-sre for post-canary watch and rollback playbook if we see memory pressure spikes.
